articles.title: GQG sale of Adani Energy shares said to disrupt hedge fund bets
articles.content: GQG Partners’ Adani Energy Solutions stake sale added unexpected supply during MSCI’s rebalancing auction, overwhelming passive-fund demand and contributing to a 10% stock decline. Hedge funds positioned for index-driven buying were also affected. About $569 million of shares changed hands, while GQG’s stake had fallen to 3.46% by August-end.

articles.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sees crude oil as low as $40 post-Iran war, lower bond yields
articles.content: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent anticipates oil prices will fall significantly after the Iran conflict concludes. He expects crude oil to reach as low as forty dollars a barrel due to oversupply. This decline in oil prices will subsequently lower bond yields, which have recently surged. Bessent also downplayed Norway's sovereign wealth fund proposal to reduce Treasury holdings.

articles.title: Rentomojo set to go public at Rs 4,246 crore valuation, set to raise Rs 1,256 crore via IPO
articles.content: In its ambitious IPO initiative, Rentomojo targets a valuation of ₹4,246 crore, while securing ₹150 crore in fresh funding. Additionally, existing investors plan to divest shares valued at ₹1,106 crore through an offer for sale. Impressively, the startup reported a 142% jump in net profit, which reached ₹104.3 crore in FY26. Mark your calendars, as the IPO launches on September 9.

articles.title: Capital market stocks rise on CAS fix hopes, index closes 1% higher
articles.content: Capital market stocks saw gains Friday after regulator Sebi's circular on the Closing Auction Session mechanism.  Trader pushback against CAS-linked settlement pricing prompted Sebi to respond to market concerns.  Erratic settlement prints since August 3 caused option premiums to swing significantly.  Market participants anticipate Sebi's paper will reduce reliance on the single CAS print.  This move is expected to restore trader confidence and remove trading volume overhang.

articles.title: No tax tangle, FPIs keen to move G-Sec money next day
articles.content: Foreign investors are advocating for expedited remittance processes after the Indian government introduced tax exemptions on bonds. They are calling on regulators and banks to enhance the speed of money transfers. This initiative aims to streamline remittance operations and mitigate settlement delays, as the exemption abolishes withholding taxes on interest and capital gains from these investments, improving market efficiency for foreign portfolio investors.

articles.title: RBI turns to longer-dated VRRR for liquidity mop-up
articles.content: In an effort to control escalating inflation, the Reserve Bank of India is running auctions to draw in surplus liquidity from the financial system. This move comes as call money rates fall beneath the policy repo rate, with predictions indicating liquidity levels could exceed fifteen lakh crore by the close of September. Additionally, the central bank recently sold government securities worth thirty-two thousand crore.

articles.title: Dollar bounces on job gains, then pares ahead of CPI
articles.content: The U.S. job market showed surprising resilience in August, adding 162,000 positions—far beyond what analysts anticipated. This result has led to heightened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase in September. However, the dollar softened slightly as traders now focus on looming inflation reports. Wages saw a year-over-year uptick of 3.1%, the weakest growth since June 2021, while the yen appreciated against the dollar throughout the week.

articles.title: Gold slides after robust US payrolls boosts rate hike bets
articles.content: Gold prices experienced a downturn on Friday, setting the stage for a weekly loss as solid US job data raised the bar for anticipated rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. This shift has rendered the non-yielding precious metal less desirable. Alongside gold, silver and platinum also saw drops. Investors are now keenly awaiting inflation updates for insights into policy adjustments.

articles.title: Oil ends week higher on renewed US-Iran strikes, diesel hits record
articles.content: Oil prices have surged dramatically this week amidst escalating military tensions between the U.S. and Iran. Record-high retail diesel prices in the U.S. are fueling global inflation concerns. Supply chain disruptions in the Middle East are dealing a blow to crude oil futures. Analysts warn of potential further increases if the conflict deepens. Additionally, positive U.S. employment figures could encourage the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates soon.
